rv.q: It's a relief, even a thrill, to slough away the imitation adolescence we settle for so often onstage and perceive the real, awkward, thoughtful thing itself.
The Saviors feels nothing like Well, I'll Let You Go. It's distinctively its own thing – yet, it's equally tense, affecting, and funny.

rv.q: The new play from Bubba Weiler is another can't-miss excavation of the heart.
Howe and Rinzel's portraits of altar boys at a crossroads are filled with life, even if the other elements of The Saviors don't feel completely fleshed out.
At only 90 minutes, 'The Saviors' is one of those new plays that makes us wish there was more of it. And the brevity here is only half the problem.
